Others leave a lasting mark on the people,
standards and industries around them.

Honorary Fellow of the Project Controls
Institute is a board-conferred recognition
for distinguished professional
contribution, leadership and service.

It involves no examination, and is separate
from PCI's examined certifications.

Every application is considered
individually, and recognition is conferred
solely at the Board's discretion.

It is intended for experienced leaders
whose impact spans project controls, cost
engineering, finance, project management
or a closely related discipline.

Applicants come from infrastructure,
energy, technology, aviation, project
finance, government and academia.

And every sector where strong
professional leadership shapes outcomes.

To be considered, applicants need at
least eight years of relevant experience,
including three at managerial level.

And a demonstrable record of
distinguished contribution. Meeting these
criteria does not guarantee recognition.

Applicants provide a professional
profile, résumé, qualifications,
career history and evidence of
contribution, for confidential review.

PCI charges no nomination,
assessment or credential fee.

Those selected are recognised as an
Honorary Fellow — recorded so anyone
can verify it at source, and labelled
honorary, never a passed examination.

Accepted applicants may also receive access
to the PCI student portal, study through
Certuvo, and invitations to selected PCI AI
events, subject to programme terms.

You may also indicate whether your
contribution aligns with project controls,
project finance or project management.

If your leadership has advanced
the profession, your contribution
deserves consideration.
Apply for Honorary Fellow PCI at pciai.org.
